title: Coherence of the relative product
statement:
Fix primes $p_0\ne\ell$, an integer $a\geq1$, $q_0=p_0^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_{q_0}$, and $k=\overline{k_0}$. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\geq1$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, choose $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$, and fix a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] with these parameters and the canonical exchange and projection transformations specified there. Integral pullbacks and tensors are completed; the field stages use rationalization and common finite coefficient fields.
Let $B$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and $f:X\to B$, $g:Y\to B$ separated finite-type morphisms. Write $T=X\times_BY$, $p:T\to X$, $q:T\to Y$, $t=fp=gq$, and $K\boxtimes L=Lp^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda Lq^*L$ for $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$. Let $\kappa_{f,g}:Rt_!(K\boxtimes L)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_!K\otimes^L_\Lambda Rg_!L$ be exactly the canonical composite of [thm-sf-kunneth-relative], with projection transformations [def-sf-pf]. Then:

(i) Under the swap $s:X\times_BY\xrightarrow{\sim}Y\times_BX$, the external-product symmetry and the symmetry $\sigma$ on the target identify $\kappa_{g,f}(L,K)$ with $\sigma\circ\kappa_{f,g}(K,L)$, including the Koszul signs.

(ii) If $h:W\to B$ is separated finite type and $M\in D^b_{ctf}(W,\Lambda)$, the two iterations of $\kappa$ on $X\times_BY\times_BW$ agree after the canonical fibre-product and derived-tensor associativity identifications.

(iii) For $b:B'\to B$ with $B'$ a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, pullback $Lb^*$ of $\kappa_{f,g}$ agrees with $\kappa$ for the base-changed data, through the compact-support exchanges for $f,g,t$ and the monoidal pullback comparisons.

(iv) For $Y=B$, $g=\mathrm{id}_B$, the canonical identifications give $\kappa_{f,\mathrm{id}}(K,L)=\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}^{-1}$.

Consequently the iterated $r$-fold products ($r\geq1$) are independent of parenthesization and order after the canonical associators and symmetries, and these compatibilities hold also for the closed-subscheme compact-support forms of [thm-sf-kunneth-relative].

proof.text: Reverse the six arrows of [thm-sf-kunneth-relative]: $\kappa^{-1}=\lambda=\alpha_{g,q}Rg_!(\beta_{f,g})\Psi_g$, where $\beta=\operatorname{PF}_q(\operatorname{Ex}_{f,g}\otimes1)$ and $\Psi_g=Rg_!(\sigma)\operatorname{PF}_g\sigma$. These are exactly the words specified in the three new lemmas.

For proper factors, [lem-sf-proper-product-counit-transpose] gives the two-counit transpose. Naturality of the signed symmetry through [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] identifies its swapped version; injectivity of the adjunction bijection [fix-prop-adjunctions] gives (i). The two triple transposes in [lem-sf-proper-triple-counit-transpose] agree, giving (ii) for proper factors by the same bijection.

source.place: Assembly of Clause (ii), associativity of tensor with PF, and final two-counit sentence: returned steps 2--4, extracting the proper three-counit transpose computation.

proof.text: For general factors, the pair identity [lem-sf-product-compactification-identity] and its completed and field forms [lem-sf-integral-open-product-diagram-normalization] reduce (i) to proper symmetry and the signed symmetry of the normalized open comparison [lem-sf-open-external-tensor-normalization]. For (ii), [lem-sf-triple-compactification-normal-form] writes each iterate as its proper iterate followed by $Rc_*e_L$ or $Rc_*e_R$; step 2 and $e_L=e_R$ identify them. This uses strict-diagram equalities before $R\lim$ integrally.

source.place: Proper reduction via product compactifications, all coefficients

proof.text: For (iii), substitute the middle-square equality [lem-sf-middle-exchange-projection-base-change] into the word of step 1. The PF base-change square [prop-sf-pf-coherence] for $g$ transports $\Psi_g$, with its symmetries transported by [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. Vertical exchange pasting, including $\alpha$, in [fix-lem-exchanges](2) combines the $g,q$ exchanges into the $t$ exchange. The resulting word is $\alpha_{g',q'}Rg'_!(\beta_{f',g'})\Psi_{g'}$; invert to obtain (iii).

source.place: Clause (iii), outer PF and composition pasting

proof.text: For (iv), $X\times_BB=X$, $p=1$, $q=f$. Identity composition [thm-sf-comp-composition], transported in [fix-lem-exchanges](2), the identity-square exchange there, and identity PF [prop-sf-pf-coherence] reduce step 1 to $\lambda=\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$: the two symmetries in $\Psi_1$ cancel. Invert.

For $r=1$ take the identity. Repeated rotations $A(BC)\leftrightarrow(AB)C$ and adjacent swaps give every bracketing and order; (ii) and (i) preserve the map. The datum's symmetric monoidal constraints [def-sf-datum] give involution, disjoint-swap and braid relations. Apply this to the restricted objects and structure maps of the closed subschemes in [thm-sf-kunneth-relative]; the symmetric associative pullback comparisons [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] identify their external products.

source.place: Consequence: finite products and closed restrictions
